plot: On Grumpy's first day off in twenty years, tucked under Bertha's blanket while Bolt promises to do his jobs, someone keeps doing every tow job first (Hal's spilled apple crates, cones round a puddle, the park's leaves); Turbo is cleared because he has no hook, Bertha swears Grumpy never left, but hook marks lead to the depot's open back window, the 'Grumpy' under the blanket is a pile of tyres, and the squeak of his old hook (planted at breakfast) gives him away: he doesn't know how to rest, so the friends teach him cloud-watching by the leaf pile; then Hal says he got the library job but can't park when people watch.

script.title: Who Is Doing Grumpy's Job?
script.description: Grumpy has his first day off in twenty years, but someone keeps doing all his jobs. Inspector Bolt #33

set.place: Wheelburg town road, Bakery Lane, Bertha's bus depot and Wheelburg Park, a sunny autumn Saturday from breakfast until late afternoon

beats.say: Bolt, hurry! Hal's apple crates fell all over the road!
They're already stacked. Neatly. But Grumpy has the day off!
I went to get help. Somebody stacked them in two minutes!
Who helps like that? Only Grumpy helps like that!
It was a sunny autumn Saturday. Let's go back to breakfast.
Lap fifty! That mystery racer never lost a race. Neither will I!
Turbo trained all week for the racer from Grandma Rosa's letter.
But at the school crossing, somebody was very, very tired.
Yaaawn. I'm not tired. My hook is tired.
His old tow hook gave a tiny squeak. Eeek.
Grumpy! When did you last have a day off?
Day off. Hmm. Nineteen... no. Twenty years ago.
TWENTY YEARS?! Today you rest. Doctor Bertha's orders!
But who tows the cars? Who puts out the cones?
I will. Just for today. Procedure.
Rest. How do you even do that?
Bertha took Grumpy to her depot. With her softest blanket.
Close your eyes. Think of clouds. I'll sit by the door.
Fine. I'm resting. I'm resting very hard. Is it done yet?
Not yet, sweetie. Resting takes all day.
Now, back on the road, Bolt studied the neat crates.
Someone strong. Someone careful. Someone who helps without a word.
Thank you, mystery helper! Wherever you are!
Wait. Did you hear that? A tiny squeak!
But Turbo zoomed in. Vroom! Nobody could hear a thing.
Does somebody need help? I'm fast! I'm here! Lap fifty-one!
Oh! And there's a big puddle on Bakery Lane. With cones!
Cones? I didn't put any cones there.
Three orange cones stood round the puddle. In a perfect circle.
Now kids can splash around it, not into it! So clever!
Strong. Careful. And now, very neat.
I promised Grumpy I'd do his jobs. Someone keeps beating me!
And if Grumpy finds out, he'll jump out of bed!
Then we solve this before he does. Quietly.
Turbo, you're everywhere today. Was it you?
Me? Look at me. No hook! I can't carry cones!
True. Our helper lifts heavy things. Our helper has a hook.
I have a winch. But I was with you all morning!
Then who else has a hook? Only Grumpy!
Everyone hurried to Bertha's depot. Without one single honk.
Shhh! He's sleeping. I've watched this door all morning.
Under the blanket was a big grey shape. Very, very still.
See? Not one wiggle. He's resting like a champion.
Then it isn't Grumpy. Hmm. Now I'm really puzzled.
Then a shout came from the park. Leaves everywhere!
Finally! A job for me! Leaves are my speciality.
Bolt zoomed to the park as fast as he could.
But the leaves were already raked. Into one giant pile.
Done. Again! I didn't even get to rake one leaf!
Wow. That's the neatest leaf pile I've ever seen!
Bolt! Look at the ground! Little marks, like a dragged hook!
The little hook marks went all the way across the park.
They lead back to Bertha's depot. To the back of it.
Bolt and Pip crept round to the back. Very quietly.
The back window is open! Wide open!
Bertha, may we look under the blanket? Very gently.
Gently, please. He needs his rest.
Bolt lifted the blanket. Under it was a pile of old tyres!
Tyres?! I watched the front door! He used the back window!
Then, behind them, came a tiny squeak. Eeek. Eeek.
Oh. Hello. I was... resting. Very fast resting.
Grumpy! YOU were the mystery helper?!
The apples, the cones, the leaves! It was you!
Your old hook gave you away. Eeek. Every time.
I tried to rest. I lay there. And lay there.
If I'm not helping, I'm just a grey truck in a blanket.
Oh, Grumpy. You're our friend. Even when you do nothing.
Resting is easy! I'll show you. It's my best thing!
So everyone drove to the park, beside the giant leaf pile.
Now look up. What does that cloud look like?
A race car! A really fast one!
That one looks like a tow hook. A sleepy one.
And for the first time in twenty years, Grumpy yawned and smiled.
Even helpers need rest. Tired helpers can't help anyone.
Tomorrow I rest again. Maybe. Probably.
Then Hal rolled up, very excited. And a little worried.
Good news! I got the job delivering library books!
But I have to park on Main Street. In front of everyone.
Why is that bad, Hal?
Because when people watch... I can't park at all.
What do you think Bolt will find next time? We'll find out in the next episode!
